name: Pular (Fula, Guinea)
notes: Pular, the Fula (ff) variety of the Fouta Djallon region of Guinea, spoken by ~4.3 million people (~55% of Guinea's population); also used in Guinea-Bissau, Sierra Leone, Mali and Senegal. Inherits the shared Fula grapheme/allophone inventory from ff.json (graphemes_base/allophones_base) since no source consulted documents a Pular-specific letter-to-IPA divergence from the pan-Fula orthography (implosives ɓ/ɗ/ƴ, prenasalized mb/nd/ng/nj, contrastive vowel length). The one well-attested difference from other Fula varieties is MORPHOLOGICAL, not phonemic or orthographic: Pular lacks the initial-consonant grade mutation between singular and plural noun classes that characterizes e.g. Pulaar (Senegal) — out of scope for a grapheme/allophone spec, which describes spelling-to-sound, not morphology (AGENTS.md §4). Also written historically in Ajami (Arabic-based) and, since the late 1980s, in the indigenous Adlam script; this spec covers only the modern Latin orthography (official since 1989), the same scope as the parent ff spec. Quality:research reflects that the child spec's own orthographic claims (beyond straight ff inheritance) are not independently sourced.
